items.headline: Dow fell 1.2% Friday; markets closed for the weekend
items.note: Friday's close (the latest trading day): the Dow fell 1.18% to 52,241.55, the S&P 500 lost 0.43% to 7,629.92 and the Nasdaq slipped 0.08% to 25,986.95. Worries about the cost of financing heavy AI spending lingered, telecom stocks fell and energy hit a record high.

items.headline: Oil jumps, consumer mood near a record low, Fed meets Wednesday
items.note: Brent crude hit its highest level since late April after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, and consumer sentiment edged down to near a record low in October. The Fed is expected to hold rates steady Wednesday, and Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon report earnings next week.

items.headline: Anthropic reportedly told investors Q3 revenue hit $16.8B, growth slowing
items.note: Reuters, citing an investor at a pre-IPO meeting, reports Q3 revenue of about $16.8B, up about 45% from Q2, a slower pace than earlier quarters. The figures are unaudited and unpublished, and the IPO is reportedly aimed at November. They differ from the draft-prospectus numbers reported yesterday, so treat all as unconfirmed until a filing appears.

items.headline: AI/ML job postings up 88% year over year, Dice says
items.note: Dice's September report says overall tech postings rose 9% from August and 17% from a year earlier, while AI and machine learning postings grew about 88% year over year. Good news for ML internship hunting, though postings are not the same as hires.

items.headline: AI finds two decades-old PHP flaws; NSA says patch now
items.note: Two critical bugs present since PHP 5 (2004) were found with help from GPT-5.6 Sol and Google's Wiz agents. No in-the-wild exploits had been reported, but the NSA says to patch or take unpatched sites offline. AI-driven security work is a growing area for ML people.

items.headline: OpenAI's Decisions API goes generally available
items.note: Per an AI news digest summarizing OpenAI's announcement, the endpoint, powered by GPT-6 Luna, returns a probability, choice or score instead of text, and is up to 10x faster than using Luna through the Responses API. It points to LLMs being used as fast classifiers inside products.

items.headline: Modal raises $750M at a $16B valuation
items.note: Per the same digest, the serverless GPU platform passed a $1B run rate and says usage has tripled since its last round five months ago. Demand for AI infrastructure startups is still strong, a useful place to look for ML engineering roles.

items.headline: Telecom stocks sink on report SpaceX wants a fourth carrier
items.note: AT&T and T-Mobile fell more than 6% and Verizon 1.6% Friday after a report that SpaceX is seeking cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier. Cell tower operators gained.

items.headline: American Express to cut 5% of its workforce
items.note: The company announced the cuts even as it raised its profit forecast, and its stock fell 3.9%. Finance firms are trimming staff while still earning well, which matters when you target finance-adjacent data roles.

learn.explain: A company's valuation is what investors collectively think the whole business is worth. For a public company that is its market cap, updated every second as the stock trades. For a private startup it is set in funding rounds: if investors put in $750M and get a slice of the company, the price they agree on implies a valuation, like Modal's reported $16B. Private valuations are negotiated, not tested daily by the market, so they can shift a lot at an IPO, when the public votes with real trades.
learn.try: Divide Modal's $16B valuation by its reported $1B run rate to get a rough price-to-sales multiple.
